      "observations": [
        "The complete six-file owned diff is read. It adds an extern-C module-creation bridge, crate-visible standalone NTLM helper, NTLM password-alert dispatch, public password failure helper, and Vec-valued response headers. No test file changes or direct helper tests appear in the checked owned modules.",
        "authenticate initializes a Gecko NTLM module, sends a small GET with a first token, chooses a case-insensitive ntlm-space-prefixed WWW-Authenticate value from the header vector, decodes the challenge, sends the second GET, and returns Failure only for final401. Any other status is Success; it does not require200, call error_from_status or inspect a cookie. The prose about a stored cookie is an expected protocol effect, not an observed result.",
        "The input Vec stays in scope while its raw pointer is used, which matches the nearby lifetime comment. Output handling is different: GetNextToken writes a raw pointer and length; slice::from_raw_parts creates a borrowed byte slice; base64 encoding creates a separate String. No free or owning allocation wrapper appears before return. The claim that Rust automatically frees that native output is unsupported by the owned implementation. A later unpaired Gecko IDL contract check is retained privately, not as an exact2025 pairing or public source record. No measured leak or current defect is claimed.",
        "The C creation bridge explicitly returns NS_ERROR_INVALID_ARG for a null module and transfers the reference only on success. That non-null module contract supports getter_addrefs; it does not establish the output token pointer, allocation or zero-length contract. Further native implementation details remain bounded.",
        "Response::header changes String to Vec<String> by splitting the channel string at newlines. It propagates GetResponseHeader errors and does not parse every comma-combined authentication grammar. The owned caller selects the NTLM-prefixed value; a missing match or base64 error fails the helper. Current response API keeps the vector with a borrowed key parameter and a later sender attaches WWW-Authenticate values to a401 authentication error.",
        "Accepted source no longer has the manual authentication/ntlm.rs or credentials.rs module paths. The checked current provider delegates Basic and NTLM to Necko. The bridge remains, and repeated-header behavior remains consumed. This phase distinction prevents the historical raw-buffer concern or cookie flow from becoming a claim about current authentication.",
        "Manual style and naming checks distinguish NTLMAuthOutcome from nsresult errors, next_b64_token_from_auth_module from the async negotiation, and raw input lifetime from output ownership. The explanatory unsafe comment needs to match the actual owner; reviewer discussion about signed c_char representation does not establish allocation cleanup.",
        "Bug1995024 original full current0–5/end is reused once for both parts. Three attachments and landings distinguish cookie support, standalone NTLM and EWS integration; they are not independently exercised protocol outcomes.",
        "D270712 full creation-to-final timeline, both actual historical inline bodies at diff1149164, and the actual Old/New summary pair are read. Old rendered summary is empty; New explains standalone reuse and repeated headers. Reviewer asks about leading-one bytes and the author clarifies c_char signed representation while admitting limited familiarity. The owned comment changes; this is not an allocation-safety review or proof.",
        "Historical Clippy warnings include unused helper items before part3 calls them; the author reports one fix and the expected remaining warnings. Approval, completed/failed remote builds and landing with ongoing or failed builds do not prove token ownership, cookie persistence or a fresh NTLM run."
      ],

      "observations": [
        "Owned patch adds mail.graph.enabled as a false-default, always-mirrored static preference, introduces User.Read-only Graph scopes and selects them for Microsoft issuer plus graph type when the preference is enabled. The existing ews/exchange branch remains EWS-scoped. It does not add Graph autodiscovery or a Graph network client.",
        "Accepted source still has that exact Microsoft graph selection branch, but the declaration now defaults true and Graph scope strings have later MailboxFolder.ReadWrite, Mail.ReadWrite, Mail.Send and offline_access additions. Treat default/scopes as revisioned behavior. The preference is not a blanket prohibition for arbitrary extension/string-scope providers: the checked branch is specifically Microsoft scope selection.",
        "The current mail OAuth caller passes server.type and username to metadata lookup unless custom OAuth details are selected, then stores allScopes and requiredScopes. A metadata object is not a successful login or token validation. combineScopes uses a Set so duplicate scope-family values do not repeat in the returned string.",
        "Owned negative test relies on the then-false default, sets the preference true for the expected Graph object, then resets it false on its normal path. Current test explicitly sets false before the negative case because the accepted default changed, and later scope expectations differ. This patch changes provider metadata tests, not a real authentication session.",
        "Both newly added assertions omit the message argument: Assert.ok has only the negated lookup, and Assert.deepEqual has only actual/expected arguments. The nearby comments do not supply assertion messages. Scoped review suggestion: give the absent-provider and expected-scope checks nonempty expected-behavior messages containing should; the negative result can use a scalar assertion and the positive object a deep assertion. No unrelated assertions are included.",
        "Manual style: early returns handle missing type/provider/scope, protocol and scope-group names are concrete, and the new branch is separated from result construction. The data objects and per-test preference changes preserve their local roles; browser pushPrefEnv requirements are not exported to this xpcshell task.",
        "Full Bug 1995822 and D270914 preserve the hidden Graph-login goal and manual bearer-token procedure, which still names an older experimental preference spelling. No token, credential, network window or curl operation was used. Review requested local test preference changes and a default-disabled check; author reports adding both. The deepEqual/negation suggestion remains Not Done; actual source retains the boolean negative assertion. All three submitted inline bodies and two old views were already read in the collector."
